messages:
Maria: heads up — saw a sharp wear counter + write-latency spike on a subset of ephemeral nvme nodes in ap-southeast1 at ~00:12 UTC, coinciding with a regional network flap. GPU attach failures started around the same time. hold on provisioning.
Alex: can you paste the nvme stats? which kernel / fw version?
Maria: iostat + nvme-smart from a representative host: 
Maria: ```
Device: nvme0n1 tps=120.3 Blk_read/s=0.0 Blk_wrtn/s=52123.4
nvme smart-log: critical_warning=0 temperature=46 ctrl_busy_time=6700
media_errors=0 wear_leveling=78% percent_used=18
```
Alex: interesting — percent_used is fine but write latency shows big tail. network logs show flaps to metadata service at 00:11:30 -> 00:12:20. likely janitor/cleaner hit backpressure and retried heavy writes. :thinking:
InfraBot: alert: ap-southeast1 ephemeral-nvme write-latency > 200ms (6 hosts) — triggered auto-evict cooldown.
Sam: janitor backlog was ~220k objects queued at that time, cleaner rate limiter tripped (we pushed the tighter limits last week). when the metadata service hiccuped the cleaner retried and amplified write bursts.
Jia (oncall): summary: cleaner retry + metadata flap => write tail => increased write amplification => wear spike and attach failures. we should: 1) pause janitor on affected pools, 2) drain hot hosts for safe reboot, 3) enable fallback GPU routing. thoughts?
Alex: +1. quick mitigation: increase janitor backoff to 10s and pause its worker threads in ap-southeast1 for the next 30m. also bump KV cache TTL for scheduler to reduce metadata calls.
Sam: can do. scheduling a throttled rollout and pause for pools: ap-southeast1-hot1, hot2, hot3.
Maria: do we risk capacity shortage if we pause janitor? we already have attach holds.
Jia (oncall): short term: route new GPU attaches to dedicated pool in us-east1 for latency-insensitive jobs. production critical jobs can wait for ~15-30m.
Sam: cost impact if we route to dedicated? rough calc: moving 30 GPUs for 30m to dedicated ~= $65 extra. if we shift batch backlog to other region + retries maybe $120 for the hour.
Maria: ok let's prioritize safety. please run the pause and start evict/drain playbook for hosts flagged by InfraBot.
InfraBot: action: janitor pause requested by Sam. executing pause on pools: ap-southeast1-hot1,ap-southeast1-hot2,ap-southeast1-hot3.
DeployBot: deploy: cleaner-rate-limiter-config v3.1.2 -> canary in ap-southeast1 (deployer=Sam)
Alex: I'll open a quick postmortem note and capture the scrub schedule overlap with network maintenance.
Sam: postmortem note: include the tighter rate-limiter change from last week, and consider a soft-fail mode for cleaner when metadata store latency > 50ms. also add a metric for cleaner-induced write-amplification.
Maria: thanks everyone — keep me posted on drain progress.
Jia (oncall): hosts drained and reboots started at 00:28 UTC, attach success rate recovering at 00:39 UTC. will keep watch for wear counter drift.
Maria: follow-up: short-term mitigation captured, we'll discuss permanent changes in next infra-ops sync. :thumbsup:
